newsitem.title: USA: Allstate affected by insurance costs.
newsitem.headline: Allstate affected by insurance costs.

text.p: Allstate Corp. said Thursday its earnings fell in the third quarter due to losses from Hurricane Fran and as it strengthened its reserves and contributed to the California Earthquake Authority.

Allstate said earnings for the quarter fell to $292 million, or 65 cents a share, compared with $446 million, or $1 a share a year earlier. Revenues rose to $6.015 billion, compared with $5.699 billion a year earlier.

During the quarter, Allstate said it took a $207 million after-tax charge to strengthen net loss reserves for discontinued lines and coverages, including those related to asbestos and environmental exposures.

It also paid a $98 million after-tax assessment to participate in the California Earthquake Authority. The $10.5 billion authority is being set up by the state to sell earthquake insurance to homeowners.
The charges were partially offset by a $57 million after-tax benefit due to a revision in the company's policy for capitalising deferred acquisition costs.
Allstate said property-liability operating income was $172 million in the third quarter compared with $336 million in the 1995 third quarter.
After-tax catastrophe losses for the period increased to $198 million compared with $111 million in the 1995 third quarter, primarily due to the effects of Hurricane Fran.
In the life insurance business, operating income increased 27.3 percent to $98 million.

For the nine months, earnings were $1.480 billion, or $3.30 a share, compared with $1.507 billion, or $3.36 a share, a year earlier. Revenues rose to $18.242 billion from $16.943 billion a year earlier.
